mcq.QUESTION_DESC: If a queue implemented using an array has size 6 and elements [10, 20, 30, 40, 50] with front = 1 and rear = 5, what happens after enqueuing 60?
In an array-based queue of size 5, we perform these operations: enqueue(10), enqueue(20), enqueue(30), dequeue(), enqueue(40), enqueue(50), enqueue(60). What is the final state?
In an array-based queue of size N, how do you check if the queue is empty?

sq.ANSWER:
A queue in data structures is a linear collection of elements that operates on the First-In, First-Out (FIFO) principle. This means that the first element added to the queue is the first one to be removed. Queues have two ends: the rear (where elements are inserted) and the front (where elements are deleted). 

Operations associated with queues:

i. Insertion: enqueue()

The enqueue() The operation inserts an element from the back of a queue or  the tail end of a queue or the rear end of the queue.

Algorithm:

Step 1: START

Step 2: Check if the queue is full.

Step 3: If the queue is full, produce an overflow error and exit.

Step 4: If the queue is not full, increment the rear pointer to point to the next space.

Step 5: Add a data element to the queue location, where the rear is pointing.

Step 6: End the process and exit.

ii. Deletion: dequeue()

The dequeue() Operation is used to remove and return the element from the front of a queue.

Algorithm

Step 1: START

Step 2: Check if the queue is empty.

Step 3: If the queue is empty, print underflow and exit.

Step 4: If the queue is not empty, access the data where the front is pointing.

Step 5: Increment the front pointer to point to the next available data element.

Step 6: Set the front and rear as -1 for the last element.

Step 7: End the process and exit.

iii. peek()

The peek()The operation returns the value at the front end of the queue without removing it.

iv. isFull()

The isFull() operation is used to determine if the queue is full or not. A queue is said to be full if it has reached its maximum capacity and there is no more space to add new elements to it.

v. isEmpty()

The isEmpty() operation is used to check if the queue is empty or not. It returns a boolean value, true when the queue is empty, otherwise false.
sq.QUESTION_DESC: What is a queue? Explain its basic operations.

sq.ANSWER:
A queue is a linear data structure that works on the First In First Out (FIFO) principle. This means that the element that is inserted first will be removed first. In a queue, we insert elements at the rear end and remove elements from the front end.

To implement a queue using an array, we use the following:

  • An array (say int queue[SIZE]) to store the elements.
  • Two integer variables: front and rear to keep track of the queue's front and rear positions.

Initial Conditions:

  • The queue is empty when front == -1 and rear == -1.
  • On first insertion, both front and rear are set to 0.

Enqueue Operation (Insert an element):

  • Before inserting, check if the queue is full using: rear == SIZE - 1.
  • If not full:
    • If front == -1, it means it’s the first element, so set front = 0.
    • Increment rear and store the new element at queue[rear].

Pseudocode:

Enqueue(value)

{

    if (rear == SIZE - 1)

        print "Queue is Full"

    else

    {

        if (front == -1)

            front = 0

        rear = rear + 1

        queue[rear] = value

        print "Element inserted successfully"

    }

}

 

Dequeue Operation (Remove an element):

  • Before deleting, check if the queue is empty using: front == -1 || front > rear.
  • If not empty:
    • Remove the element at queue[front].
    • Increment front to point to the next element.
    • If front > rear, reset both front and rear to -1 (queue becomes empty again).

Pseudocode:

Dequeue()

{

    if (front == -1 || front > rear)

        print "Queue is Empty"

    else

    {

        value = queue[front]

        front = front + 1

        print "Deleted element:", value

 

        if (front > rear)

        {

            front = -1

            rear = -1

        }

    }

}
sq.QUESTION_DESC: Describe how a queue can be implemented using an array.

lq.ANSWER:
In this hospital scenario, each patient must be attended to in the order of their arrival. This exactly follows the FIFO (First-In, First-Out) principle. Therefore, a queue is the ideal data structure to use.

Queue Structure and Initialization:

We will use an array to store patient names and two integer variables front and rear to keep track of the queue.

#include <stdio.h>

#include <string.h>

#define SIZE 100

char queue[SIZE][50];  // Array of strings to store patient names

int front = -1, rear = -1;

 

Function 1: Registering a New Patient (Enqueue)

  • If the queue is full, show a message.
  • Otherwise, insert the patient’s name at the rear of the queue.

void registerPatient(char name[]) {

    if (rear == SIZE - 1) {

        printf("Queue is full. Cannot register more patients.\n");

    } else {

        if (front == -1) front = 0;  // First registration

        rear++;

        strcpy(queue[rear], name);

        printf("Patient %s registered successfully.\n", name);

    }

}

 

Function 2: Calling the Next Patient (Dequeue)

  • If the queue is empty, notify.
  • Otherwise, remove the patient from the front of the queue.

void callNextPatient() {

    if (front == -1 || front > rear) {

        printf("No patients in the queue.\n");

    } else {

        printf("Calling patient: %s\n", queue[front]);

        front++;

        if (front > rear) {

            front = rear = -1;  // Queue becomes empty

        }

    }

}

 

Function 3: Displaying the Queue

  • If queue is empty, show that no one is waiting.
  • Otherwise, display all patients from front to rear.

void displayQueue() {

    if (front == -1 || front > rear) {

        printf("No patients waiting.\n");

    } else {

        printf("Patients waiting in queue:\n");

        for (int i = front; i <= rear; i++) {

            printf("%s\n", queue[i]);

        }

    }

}

 

Main Function

int main() {

    registerPatient("John");

    registerPatient("Mary");

    registerPatient("David");

 

    displayQueue();

 

    callNextPatient();  // Should call John

    displayQueue();     // Should show Mary and David

 

    callNextPatient();  // Should call Mary

    callNextPatient();  // Should call David

    callNextPatient();  // Should show empty

    return 0;

}

Output:

Patient John registered successfully.

Patient Mary registered successfully.

Patient David registered successfully.

Patients waiting in queue:

John

Mary

David

Calling patient: John

Patients waiting in queue:

Mary

David

Calling patient: Mary

Calling patient: David

No patients in the queue.
